What I found that works best for me whenever I have to work after a sleepless night (YMMV).

  1. I drink a lot of water, take one tea in the middle of the day. Coffee doesn't work too well.
    Water > Tea >>> Coffee
  2. I don't eat. Not at lunch and no snacks. I do eat before going to work but even then, it does make me sluggish for about the first hour and a half.
  3. I go take some air outside a few times.
Water makes me tired for some reason, I don't know why. And I already intermittent fast, so I wont eat till noon anyways. I usually manage to stay awake, but my eyes end up feeling like sandpaper :/

I'll second the tea suggestion. Hit the tea as soon as you can. Herbal tea like licorice, green or black tea, or yerba maté. Morning fasting could be part of the issue I think. I'd suggest a small liquid meal about an hour after getting out of bed. Something like this: http://orgain.com/products/original-organic-nutritional-shake/

As far as the insomnia itself there are a few basic things to try, if you haven't already:

Observe the dawn - basically setting the Circadian rhythm. Just get outside briefly at sunrise if you can.

Observe the twilight - again helping to stimulate the normal ebb and flow of melatonin, the sleep hormone.

Take a hot shower right before bed - rest is also triggered by falling body temperature. Get the shower steamy and stay in for 10 minutes at least, then dry off and lay down.

Practice bi-phasic sleep, which was the norm before electric lights. This goes well with the above steps about observing sunrise/sunset. Sleep or lay in the dark for at least 3 hours shortly after dark, then rise for 2 to 4 hours, include some light exercise like walking, perhaps a snack, then sleep again, odds are your body will let you rest then until morning.

Other than those specific tips, there's always the general health and wellness issues like stimulating the metabolism with regular exercise and maintaining a nutritious diet. Sometimes a diet missing one or two key factors like magnesium or potassium or whatever can cause vague dis-ease like fatigue and sleep issues.

Anyway good luck.

Ok, so I have these issues too. They first started when I wasn't properly managing my pain, and that would keep me up at night. A brief stint (about a year) working overnights didn't help either!

I don't drink coffee after noon, and I don't drink caffeinated tea/pop/anything else after 5pm. I usually wake up to hungry cats (no snooze button there) around 7am, and I get most of my caffeine before 10am really.

I drink plenty of water throughout the day, and work out a little every day. By that I mean I just never am completely sedentary (unless I have the flu or something). I go to the gym 4 days a week, doing a class and then the sauna or steam room, or a little recumbent bike with my 3DS and then some steam room time after - it's great for winding down.

A third tier is what I like to call mindful relaxation. Some people read before bed, some have camomile tea, some meditate... The point is, for at least the next month, be really strict about what you do the hour before you go to bed. A lot of people suggest no screen time for 2 hours before bed because they (TV, computer, phone) are too stimulating. I did this for a few months, but I can sleep next to my phone again so it doesn't have to be forever now!

Also, just meditation, foam rolling and yoga in general are great to clear the mind during the day. If you are less stressed during the day then you won't be so wound up at night.

You can keep a little notepad to help you jot down notes if that keeps you up. I always stay up the night before something exciting is happening (before a trip out party) planning out details. Before I go to bed I make a good solid list and keep it by the bed in case I think of something that I might have forgotten right as I drift off to sleep....

I hope this helps!
